_meta.source: subset of clients/lilac-insure/inbox-discovery-prompts.md — the 3 highest-value questions to validate Phase 1 priority. Add more by appending here; discovery.mjs picks them up automatically.
_meta.promptDesignNotes: Each question's prompt is run with the same data window (last N messages). The prompt instructs the LLM to return a single JSON object matching outputSchema.

questions.label: Inbox composition by category
questions.decisionItInforms: Keep / merge / split our 12 categories. If 'claim' is 0.5%, deprioritize. If 'renewal' is 35%, prioritize renewal-reminder.
questions.systemPrompt: You are an analyst summarizing email inboxes for an independent insurance agency. Output strict JSON only. Refer to insurance-industry conventions: lifecycle stages (prospect, onboarding, active, renewal, off-boarding) and ops categories (carrier-ops, vendor-ops, compliance, internal, noise).
questions.userPromptTemplate:
Below are {{count}} email metadata records (from / subject / received-at, body previews redacted to first 200 chars).

Group them into 8–12 topical buckets. For each bucket return: id (lowercase, hyphenated), label (human-readable), definition (one sentence), pct (approximate % of the sample), examples (array of up to 3 representative subject lines).

Return JSON shape: { "buckets": [ { "id", "label", "definition", "pct", "examples": [] } ], "summary": "one-sentence overall observation" }.

--- DATA ---
{{data}}

questions.label: Top sender domains
questions.decisionItInforms: Sharpens from-pattern rules in categories.json. Validates / replaces our guessed carrier and wholesaler lists.
questions.systemPrompt: You are an analyst categorizing email senders for an independent insurance agency. Output strict JSON only.
questions.userPromptTemplate:
Below are {{count}} email metadata records.

List the top 30 sender domains by message count. For each return: domain, count, kind (one of: carrier | wholesaler | vendor | client | regulator | personal | unknown), description (one sentence), typicalSubjects (up to 3).

Return JSON shape: { "domains": [ { "domain", "count", "kind", "description", "typicalSubjects": [] } ] }.

--- DATA ---
{{data}}

questions.label: Lead response time
questions.decisionItInforms: Baseline for the auto-responder SLA. If median is already 5min, auto-responder is a safety net not a value driver. If median is 4hr, it's the headline win.
questions.systemPrompt: You are an analyst measuring response times for an independent insurance agency. Output strict JSON only. Match leads (inbound, from a forms/gravity/quote-request source) to the agency's first reply.
questions.userPromptTemplate:
Below are {{count}} email metadata records, ordered by received-at.

Identify every email that looks like a lead: from `forms@`, `gravityforms`, `wordpress@`, or subject containing 'quote request' / 'new lead'. For each lead, find the first reply from the agency owner (sender domain matching `lilacinsure.com` or `hirobius.com` is suspicious; any from-domain that appears as a sender of agency-style replies is the agency).

Return JSON shape: { "leadsFound": int, "repliedTo": int, "medianResponseMinutes": number, "p90ResponseMinutes": number, "unreplied": int, "sampleLeadIds": [strings] }.

--- DATA ---
{{data}}
